Hey Voat, I wanted to share with you my personal experience of becoming a professional slacker over the last two and a half years. Not only for your reading pleasure, but also because it may contain useful information for other aspiring slackers. Typed up for you from my workplace no less. Personally, I've found I love stories about people who find ways to slack off at work.

Now, I wasn't always a slacker. Believe it or not, I was once a hardworking, job market-fearing, wage slave for the longest time. I started in fast food, finally got into retail when I was halfway through college. Every time a manager critiqued me, I worked to improve because those conversations made me feel expendable. The general attitude of the time was that you were lucky to have a job, any job. I frowned on my co-workers that stopped to play with their cellphones or held long conversations while there was still work to be done.

Then I graduated, and with my bachelor's degree managed to get a job... that did not require a bachelor's degree. Fuck I picked my major badly. I ended up in Insurance, I applied for a job position and instead ended up with a slightly lower paying position at the same company. It was pretty insulting since neither position requires a degree but whatever, everything felt like a huge improvement over retail and definitely fast food.

It turned out this was a new department the company was forming and they were still in the process of converting, which meant we had way more people than we needed and every place was not yet funneling calls into us. So at the start, this meant all we did was answer 2 or 3 calls A DAY. All we did during those calls was gather information about the accident and the people involved. You can only review the manual so much until you've got the job down, so I started bringing handheld video games in and my bosses didn't even care.

Over the course of a few months, our department finally started to get busier, the management was getting their shit together, and my video games were getting frowned on. Still plenty of time between calls, so I just switched to reading manga right on the computer I was using for work. No shits given again.

By the time we finally had enough calls coming in that we could stay busy most of the time, I had gotten used to spending most of my time not working. I seemed able to get through a call quicker than most people, so I used it to my advantage. I would spend time between calls, purposefully doing nothing even though the clock was ticking on it as "Wrap time" (time to finish filing the claim before moving onto the next call.)

Finally reading manga on the computer got frowned on. Up until then, I had never really used my cellphone for entertainment purposes, but I figured out that no one frowns upon people using it. It quickly became my personal entertainment center. My work has open wi-fi and I ended up playing video games and reading manga all over again.

By the time I promoted to the position I had originally applied for way back when, the claim filing position was so busy that they had temp workers coming in. Even once I started training for the basic claim handling position, there was a bunch of downtime where other people were slow and had to catch up. I ended up reading and writing. I was writing out roleplay posts, the connection on the computer itself had the website I used blocked, but not the wi-fi on my cellphone. For some reason the computer didn't block a free forum I set up for myself. I would review old posts on my phone, write a post on the computer, send it to myself on the free forum, then copy and paste it into the roleplay.

In my new position I was again meeting call intake and claim handling goals sooner than was expected and ended up spending a lot of time with my cellphone again. I could clear claim handling easy, since the system doesn't check if you're cherry picking easy tasks. A few months later, my cellphone was finally frowned upon. That was about the time I started visiting Voat on the computer and spending my day reading just about everything on here. However, I didn't realize my usage of Internet Explorer was being monitored until my boss mentioned it to me. I guess it was to get across the point that I can't avoid him seeing what I'm doing.

It had the opposite effect, all he could see was time I spent on non-business websites. I quickly figured out that Firefox was on my computer and he probably couldn't monitor that. I was right. Our intranet manual has a bunch of frames around the actual content, so I resized Firefox into that box so at a glance it just looked like the manual.

Our seats got shifted around recently, now my back and my monitors both face everyone walking by. I got a mirror to "decorate" my desk with, but it hasn't done me much good. My boss caught on to me using firefox (since he generally has a good view of my screen if he's walking by) and so now I'm spending my free time writing shit and sending it to my personal forum. Or browsing Voat when I know he's not around.

TL;DR I got used to a easy do-nothing job and ended up working to find every method I can to do less as work piled up.

I won't say what company I work at, in the unlikely event this comes back to bite me. But I'm open to questions, and I won't take it personally if you hard-working types are upset with me or people like me.
